COUNCIL & CROWN · v0.10.1

The classroom turn

Whole regiments. Larger territories. One decision at a time.

Play · Versions

First practice turn

Choose a country. Give one regiment a Capture land order in a neighboring empty territory and save its order. Switch countries and make their plans. Click Teacher: move everyone. At each shared territory, choose a country to attack or Hold; confirm every involved country. Offer alliances here and switch to the recipient to accept. Click Resolve combat, choose any required retreats, and finish the phase.

Results list troop losses, captures and income. Use Zoom to battle site and Download map for illustrations. Students create their own tables in Google Docs. The site does not build or export their assignment tables.

Rules

Four stages: plan orders → agree alliances and choose countries to attack → resolve combat and choose retreats → review results. Only the teacher advances. This local prototype exposes all countries to its host; it does not yet provide private student logins.

Regiments: 100 health when recruited. Spears beat cavalry; cavalry beat archers; archers beat spears. Artillery is neutral against all unit types, with normal damage in both directions. Its city-capture bonus is planned for when cities are added. Advantage ×1.5, disadvantage ×0.75. Base damage is 30% of the regiment’s current health, modified by type, travel fatigue, allies and pursuit. Damage is simultaneous. No free healing or mixing individual soldiers.

Movement: 2 territories per turn, up to 4 with research. Empty foreign land can be crossed. Hostile troops block a route through their location. Meeting during travel stops movement; opposing armies crossing the same edge meet in the lower-numbered territory. Rough territory crossed reduces attack by 15%, capped at 30%.

Country targets: choose one opponent per contested territory or hold. Each regiment attacks once; its country’s combined damage budget is shared among its opponent’s regiments in proportion to health. Several opponents add their damage before it is applied. Mutually agreed allies attacking the same opponent gain ×1.5 damage, except when that opponent attacks them back. Attacking an ally breaks that alliance after the simultaneous exchange.

Retreat: a damaged country with fewer surviving troops than the strongest force at the site must retreat one adjacent territory. Ties hold. No safe escape means surrender. Retreat preserves damage. During the next cycle, a retreat-marked regiment moving away takes ×2 damage if a previous attacker catches it again. The mark then expires.

Capture: only a capture order claims land. Ownership changes after retreats if only one country remains and it ordered capture. Disputed territory keeps its owner. Each controlled territory pays 8 money, 4 food and 8 of its local resource each turn, until captured. Recruitment costs 50 money, 20 food, and equipment; six living regiments maximum per country. Movement research costs 60 money, 15 wood and 15 metal, and takes effect next turn.

Technology: this intentionally small version retains movement research only. The more detailed economy, education, settlements and trade remain in the archived v0.9 game. Old campaign saves are kept separately; this mode starts a new campaign.

Worked damage example

Three full-health spear regiments from different countries share a territory. A and B both attack C, which holds. Without an alliance, each deals 30 damage and C has 40 health left. If A and B accepted an alliance, each deals 45 and C has 10 left. If C attacks A back, A deals its normal 30 while B deals 45; C ends with 25 health and A with 70. All losses happen together.

If C has two identical 100-health regiments instead, damage is shared between them; adding a defending unit does not duplicate the attacking country's damage budget. Different troop types, rough travel and pursuit modify the contributions before rounding.

Save and restore

Download game before class ends. Open game restores the complete campaign. Restore previous phase swaps the previous checkpoint and current state. Old detailed campaigns belong in the archived v0.9 game. Unreadable local saves pause autosave and can be downloaded; explicitly opening a backup or starting a world resumes saving.

This is teacher-hosted on one device with all countries visible. Private student orders and synchronized devices require a future multiplayer stage. The teacher buttons are workflow controls, not authenticated permissions.

Imported Full JSON provides real geometry; a PNG alone cannot describe land adjacency. Only connected land movement is included. Isolated islands have no sea route yet. Original-country territory chunks are geographically uneven; playtest costs and starting positions with your class.

Map and biome foundations: Azgaar (MIT). Voronoi geometry: D3 Delaunay (ISC). Licenses are preserved in vendor/. Earlier detailed mechanics and integration references are preserved with each frozen release.
